objective: Given a scenario, analyze network-related indicators: rogue devices, enumeration, anomalous activity, activity on unexpected ports
secondaryObjectives: Log analysis with security information and event management (SIEM), and user and entity behavior analysis (UEBA) with Open User and Entity Behavior Analytics (OpenUBA)

sources.cite: CompTIA CySA+ CS0-004 Exam Objectives, Exam Objectives Document Version 2.0 (exam launched 2026-06-23; domains 34/26/24/16)
sources.note: Relevant text: 1.2 'Given a scenario, analyze indicators of potential malicious activity' (host-related indicators: resource consumption, unauthorized software, anomalous activity: suspicious or rogue processes, Living Off the Land Binaries (LOLBins) and Scripts, file system changes, data exfiltration); 2.3 'Given a scenario, analyze data to prioritize and mitigate vulnerabilities' (exploitability, active exploitation/threat intelligence, asset value, impact, patch/remediation availability, true/false positives, true/false negatives; CVSS metrics, EPSS); 3.2 'Summarize the incident response process' (containment, recovery); 3.3 'Given a scenario, implement incident response techniques' (triage, establishment of a timeline, determining severity and impact, escalation; isolating affected targets, remediation and verification, release from isolation, performing restoration). Read in the official objectives PDF (the course's officialObjectivesUrl) through a summarizing fetch, and the CompTIA V4 page, on 2026-11-11. CS0-003 retires for English on 2026-12-22. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's alert-triage-lolbin-hunt (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the systems, the data and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the SOC analyst on the morning shift at Harrowgate Insurance, a fictional insurer. Three network alerts are waiting in the queue.
handover: Network access control can move a switch port to a quarantine VLAN.
IT runs an authorized vulnerability scan on the first Sunday of each month only.
howItWorks: The console shows the alert queue, the event log and each asset's status.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: the device captures finance staff credentials from the network for another day before anyone looks.
Check-in 3: the attacker uses what the sweep found to move to a file server.
Check-in 4: the attacker uses the beacon to stage a data upload from WS-0388 overnight.

roguePrompt.title: An unknown device on the finance floor
roguePrompt.context: It is not in the asset inventory.

choices.label: Move port 3/0/27 to the quarantine VLAN through network access control, have facilities locate the device, photograph and seize it, and record the MAC, lease and port

effects.log: The port is quarantined; a small computer is found under the meeting room table.

choices.feedback: A rogue device is contained at the port, physically located and preserved as evidence.

choices.label: Block its MAC address on the network
choices.feedback: MAC addresses are easy to change; the device can return with another.

choices.label: Close it as a new printer that IT forgot to register
choices.feedback: Nobody checked; an unknown device stays on the finance network.

sweepPrompt.title: A workstation enumerating the network
sweepPrompt.context: It is not the scheduled scan window.

choices.label: Check the scan schedule (none today), isolate WS-0412 with EDR, collect its process list and logs, and find the user and parent process that ran the scan

effects.log: WS-0412 is isolated; a scanning tool was dropped by a macro.

choices.feedback: Enumeration outside an authorized window is a likely sign of an intruder mapping the network.

choices.label: Block ports 22, 445 and 3389 from WS-0412 at the firewall

effects.log: Those ports are blocked from the host.

choices.feedback: It slows the sweep but leaves the compromised host running.

choices.label: Assume it is IT's scanner and suppress the alert
choices.feedback: The scan schedule says otherwise; the attacker keeps mapping.

beaconPrompt.title: Regular outbound traffic on port 4444
beaconPrompt.context: One connection every 60 seconds to the same address.

choices.label: Isolate WS-0388, capture its traffic and memory, block the destination at the egress firewall, and search all flows for the same address and timing

effects.log: WS-0388 is isolated; one more host shows the same beacon.

choices.feedback: Fixed-interval connections on an unexpected port suggest command and control; contain, preserve evidence and hunt for the same indicator.

choices.label: Block the destination address only
choices.feedback: The implant may switch addresses; the host stays compromised.

choices.label: Open a low-priority ticket for next week
choices.feedback: A week of command and control is a week of attacker access.

reflection.question: Write the shift record for the incident lead.

parts.label: Indicators
parts.criteria: Rogue device, unscheduled enumeration and a 60-second beacon on 4444.
parts.modelAnswer: An unknown device joined the finance floor; WS-0412 swept 1,900 addresses outside the scan window; WS-0388 beaconed to one address on 4444 every minute.

parts.label: Actions
parts.criteria: Port quarantined and device seized; hosts isolated; hunt found one more.
parts.modelAnswer: We quarantined the port and seized the device, isolated both workstations with evidence, blocked the address and found one more beaconing host.

source.note: Contained and closed within 60 minutes of the first alert.
No asset newly exposed by the response.

noProgress.rationale: Every decision only partly right leaves the work done late or incomplete but harms nothing; a cost, not harm.

scoring.modelReasoning: Network indicators need context: unknown devices are contained at the port and located; enumeration outside an authorized window is hostile until proven otherwise; regular traffic on an unexpected port suggests command and control. Contain, preserve evidence and hunt for the same indicator elsewhere.
